nodes.one_zh: 开工前先公示方法与判据
nodes.one_en: Publish method and criteria before data
nodes.def_zh: 预注册源自临床试验与心理学可重复性危机：试验开始前把假设、方法、分析计划、通过判据登记在案（如 OSF 注册），防「事后挑好看的结论」（HARKing、p-hacking）。动机：数据一到手，人的诚实就开始打折——先承诺再动手是对自己诚实的制度化。工程里对应「结构性改动前冻结设计与判据」；两者共享同一条根：判据先于证据冻结，事后解释必须让位于事前承诺。
nodes.def_en: Preregistration comes from clinical trials and psychology's reproducibility crisis: register hypothesis, methods, analysis plan, and pass criteria before the trial starts (e.g., on the OSF), preventing 'post-hoc cherry-picking' (HARKing, p-hacking). The motive: the moment data arrives, human honesty starts discounting — commit first, build second, is institutionalized self-honesty. In engineering it maps to freezing design and criteria before structural changes; both share one root: criteria freeze before evidence, and post-hoc explanation yields to prior commitment.
nodes.plain_zh: 赌局开始前把「算谁赢」写在公证处，而不是看完成绩再定规则。临床试验几十年血泪：先看数据再定标准的研究，结论总能「变好」——所以规矩改成先押注后开奖。
nodes.plain_en: Write 'who wins' at the notary BEFORE the game starts, not after seeing the scores. Decades of clinical-trial scar tissue: studies that set standards after seeing data always 'improve' — so the rule became bet first, draw cards second.
nodes.example_zh: 心理学界的标志性案例：预注册与不预注册的同类研究，效应量系统性差一截（许多 p<0.05 的结果复现失败）——这就是 goldmine 把「判负即回滚」写进流程的方法源头。
nodes.example_en: The field's landmark finding: the same hypotheses studied with and without preregistration show systematically different effect sizes (many p<0.05 results failed replication) — the methodological root of goldmine writing 'a loss is a rollback' into its process.

nodes.one_zh: 键排序去空白，键序不同不算不同
nodes.one_en: Sort keys; order stops mattering
nodes.def_zh: 把 JSON 的键递归排序、去掉无关空白后序列化为确定字节串再哈希。这样 {"a":1,"b":2} 与 {"b":2,"a":1} 得到同一身份——语义相同的配置不该因为序列化顺序的巧合而分裂向量家族。这是分布式系统与密码工程的通用手法（canonical serialization）：凡「要被哈希/签名的结构化数据」，先定义其规范形，再谈身份。tests/test_fingerprints.py 的 test_id_stable_across_key_order 钉死这条性质。
nodes.def_en: Keys are recursively sorted and insignificant whitespace stripped, producing deterministic bytes to hash. {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1} then share one identity — semantically identical configs must not split into two vector families by serialization accident. A universal move in distributed systems and cryptographic engineering (canonical serialization): for any structured data to be hashed or signed, define its canonical form before talking about identity. tests/test_fingerprints.py's test_id_stable_across_key_order pins this property.
nodes.plain_zh: 两张购物清单，一张按拼音排、一张随手写，买的东西一模一样就该算同一张单子。先统一按字母排序再比对，顺序就再也搅不了局。
nodes.plain_en: Two shopping lists — one alphabetized, one scribbled — buying exactly the same things should count as the same list. Sort both alphabetically before comparing, and order can never cause trouble again.
nodes.example_zh: goldmine/fingerprints.py 的 canonical()：keys=sorted + 无空白 separators，产出字节串供 sha256。测试 test_id_stable_across_key_order 明确验证键序不同 → 指纹相同。
nodes.example_en: goldmine/fingerprints.py's canonical(): keys=sorted plus whitespace-free separators, yielding bytes for sha256. The test test_id_stable_across_key_order explicitly verifies different key orders → identical fingerprint.

nodes.one_zh: 各干各的分支，合并经评审
nodes.one_en: Isolated branches, merges through review
nodes.def_zh: 版本控制的分支方法：每条工作线在自己的分支上提交，主线只经评审/验收合入。价值有二：并行工作互不踩踏（写者隔离）；变更以「可评审的单元」进入主线（合并即评审点）。本项目的实例化：一会话一分支 + 合并经用户 + stash A/B 归因。方法源头从 CVS 年代到 git flow/trunk-based 演化多年，共识始终是「隔离线 + 受控合入」。
nodes.def_en: The version-control method of branching: each line of work commits on its own branch, and the mainline receives changes only through review/acceptance. Two values: parallel work never tramples (writer isolation), and changes enter the mainline as reviewable units (the merge IS the review point). This project's instantiation: one session one branch + merges through the user + stash A/B attribution. The method evolved from CVS through git flow to trunk-based, with one constant: isolated lines, controlled merges.
nodes.plain_zh: 装修队各占一面墙刷，刷完请房东挨面验收再算「完工」。谁的活儿谁认领：出问题先看是谁的墙，不会一笔糊涂账。
nodes.plain_en: Painters each take a wall; the landlord inspects wall by wall before anything counts as 'done'. Whose wall, whose account: a problem maps straight to its owner, never a muddled ledger.
nodes.example_zh: 撞车事件的归因实验就是分支方法的应用：git stash 掉对方改动 → 重跑测试 → 全绿即归因成立——隔离线让「谁的改动导致失败」变成可实验的问题。
nodes.example_en: The collision's attribution drill is branching applied: git stash the other session's changes → rerun tests → all green means attribution confirmed — isolation turns 'whose change broke it' into an experiment.

nodes.one_zh: 独立审稿人专找反面证据
nodes.one_en: Independent reviewers hunt counter-evidence
nodes.def_zh: 科学界的质量机制：独立于作者的评审人专职攻击稿件（找反例、验主张、查统计），裁决接受/修改/拒绝。要点有三：独立性（评审人不与作者共谋）、对抗性（职责是找错不是捧场）、结构化裁决（有限选项，不许客套话）。本项目的实例化是对抗评审（另一个 AI 上下文，ADOPT/ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES/REJECT）与「合并经用户」；方法上的共同点：把「自查」升级为「异查」。
nodes.def_en: Science's quality mechanism: reviewers independent of the author exist to attack the manuscript (hunt counterexamples, verify claims, check statistics) and rule accept/revise/reject. Three essentials: independence (reviewers don't conspire with authors), adversarial duty (the job is finding flaws, not applause), and structured verdicts (a few options, no pleasantries). This project's instantiations: adversarial review (another AI context, ADOPT/ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES/REJECT) and 'merges through the user' — methodologically, upgrading self-review to other-review.
nodes.plain_zh: 论文投出去不是让朋友夸，是请三位陌生专家专门找茬：数据撑得起结论吗？有没有反例？统计过关吗？他们的职责就是让错误活不过投稿这一关。
nodes.plain_en: Submitting a paper isn't asking friends for praise — it's hiring three strangers to hunt flaws: do the data carry the conclusion? Any counterexamples? Does the statistics pass? Their job is making errors die at submission.
nodes.example_zh: 本项目的两次关键拦截（21 个离线测试、版本字面量漂移）都是「异查」抓到「自查」漏掉的问题——评审者的独立性比聪明更重要。
nodes.example_en: This project's two key interceptions (the 21 offline tests, the version-literal drift) were both flaws 'other-review' caught and 'self-review' missed — the reviewer's independence matters more than cleverness.
nodes.analogy_zh: 请三位陌生专家专门找茬，不请朋友捧场
nodes.analogy_en: Three strangers hired to find flaws, not friends for applause

nodes.one_zh: 每个意思都是空间里的一个点
nodes.one_en: Every idea is a point in space
nodes.def_zh: 向量 = 一组有序的数（分量），可看作高维空间里从原点出发的一个箭头：2 个分量是平面，3 个是房间，768 个只是继续加轴。两个箭头可以相加、相减、数乘，更重要的可以量夹角与距离——所有向量检索的数学都建立在这几个操作上。「维数高」不神秘：它只是「用很多个数描述一个东西」。
nodes.def_en: A vector is an ordered list of numbers (components), viewable as an arrow from the origin in a high-dimensional space: 2 components make a plane, 3 a room, 768 merely keeps adding axes. Arrows add, subtract, scale — and, most importantly, admit angles and distances. All vector-retrieval math stands on these few operations. 'High-dimensional' is no mystery: it just means 'describe a thing with many numbers'.
nodes.plain_zh: 用几个数说清一个位置：教室里第几排第几列是两个数；城市里经度纬度海拔是三个数。说一个「意思」用了 768 个数——听起来吓人，其实就是把「第几排第几列」问了很多很多遍。
nodes.plain_en: Describe a position with numbers: row and seat in a classroom take two; longitude, latitude, altitude take three. Describing a 'meaning' takes 768 numbers — sounds scary, but it's just asking 'which row, which seat' many, many more times.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算：平面上的点 (3,4) 到原点距离 = √(3²+4²) = 5（勾股定理）。768 维同理，只是把 768 个平方加起来再开方——公式没变，轴变多了。
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: the point (3,4) sits at distance √(3²+4²) = 5 from the origin (Pythagoras). 768 dimensions work the same — sum 768 squares, take the root; the formula never changed, only the axes multiplied.
nodes.analogy_zh: 「第几排第几列」问 768 遍
nodes.analogy_en: 'Which row, which seat' asked 768 times

deep.rel_zh: 点定了，怎么量两点的关系
deep.rel_en: Points fixed — how to relate two of them

nodes.one_zh: 距离量幅度，夹角量方向
nodes.one_en: Distance measures size, angle measures direction
nodes.def_zh: 比较两个向量的两种基本量：欧氏距离（箭头尖到尖的直线长度，对向量的「大小」敏感）与夹角（两条箭头张开多少度，只看「方向」）。归一化向量上两者等价；未归一化时含义不同——文本嵌入里长度多对应文本长短/信息量，方向才对应含义，所以语义比较选夹角（余弦）。
nodes.def_en: Two basic quantities for comparing vectors: Euclidean distance (tip-to-tip straight length, sensitive to 'size') and angle (how far the arrows spread, pure 'direction'). On normalized vectors they are equivalent; otherwise they mean different things — in text embeddings, length mostly tracks text length or information bulk while direction carries meaning, so semantic comparison picks the angle (cosine).
nodes.plain_zh: 两支手电筒：一支大手电一支小手电，都照向同一棵树。论光柱长短（距离）它俩差很远；论照的方向（夹角）它俩一模一样。找「意思相近」的东西，该比方向，不是比亮度。
nodes.plain_en: Two flashlights — one big, one small — both aimed at the same tree. By beam length (distance) they differ hugely; by aim (angle) they're identical. Finding 'similar meaning' compares aim, not brightness.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算：向量 (1,0) 与 (2,0)——距离 = 1，夹角 = 0°（余弦 1）。同样的方向、不同的长度：距离变了，夹角没变。这就是「长短不同不影响含义相近」的几何版本。
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: vectors (1,0) and (2,0) — distance = 1, angle = 0° (cosine 1). Same direction, different length: distance moved, angle didn't. That is the geometric version of 'length doesn't change meaning'.
nodes.analogy_zh: 大手电小手电都照同一棵树：比方向不比亮度
nodes.analogy_en: Big and small flashlights on one tree: compare aim, not brightness

deep.rel_zh: 夹角与距离都住在同一张地图上
deep.rel_en: Both live on the same map

nodes.one_zh: 词指向含它的行，像书后索引
nodes.one_en: Word to rows, like a book's index
nodes.def_zh: 正排是「文档 → 它含哪些词」；倒排把它反过来：「词 → 哪些文档含它」。查询时不用扫全部文档，只查查询词对应的那几个 posting list。这是全文检索几十年的地基（Lucene、SQLite FTS5 都是它），BM25 之类的排名函数就跑在 posting list 上。
nodes.def_en: A forward index maps 'document → its words'; the inverted index flips it: 'word → which documents contain it'. A query never scans all documents — it consults just the posting lists of its query words. This has been full-text search's foundation for decades (Lucene, SQLite FTS5 alike), and ranking functions like BM25 run on those posting lists.
nodes.plain_zh: 书后的索引页就是倒排索引：正文是「第 3 页有哪些词」（正排），索引页反过来「『垫片』出现在第 3、47、102 页」。查词翻索引，不用一页页读全书。
nodes.plain_en: A book's back index IS an inverted index: the body says 'page 3 contains these words' (forward); the index flips it — ''gasket': pages 3, 47, 102'. Look up a word by flipping the index, not by reading the book.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算：三篇文档 D1={a,b}、D2={b,c}、D3={a,c}。倒排后 a→{D1,D3}、b→{D1,D2}、c→{D2,D3}。查「b」只碰两个 posting 项，不碰 D3——文档越多省得越多。
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: three docs D1={a,b}, D2={b,c}, D3={a,c}. Inverted: a→{D1,D3}, b→{D1,D2}, c→{D2,D3}. Querying 'b' touches two postings and never D3 — the bigger the corpus, the bigger the saving.
nodes.analogy_zh: 书后的索引页就是它本尊
nodes.analogy_en: The book's back index, in person

nodes.one_zh: 平均分与波动幅度两把基准尺
nodes.one_en: The average and the spread
nodes.def_zh: 均值 = 所有数相加除以个数（重心）；标准差 = 每个数偏离均值的典型幅度（方差的平方根）。二者合起来回答「这个数在这个群体里正常吗」：高出均值几个标准差就有几个 z。它是从考试分数到实验测量再到音频响度（RMS 是能量版的均值）通用的描述统计底座。
nodes.def_en: The mean is the sum divided by the count (the center of mass); the standard deviation is the typical deviation from that mean (the square root of variance). Together they answer 'is this value normal for this group': so many standard deviations above the mean, so many z's. The descriptive-statistics bedrock of everything from exam scores to lab measurements to audio loudness (RMS is the energy-flavored mean).
nodes.plain_zh: 先算全班平均分，再看大家离平均分平均有多远——前者是「平常什么样」，后者是「波动多大」。知道这两件事，任何一个分数你都能说清它是「正常」还是「离谱」。
nodes.plain_en: First the class average, then how far everyone typically sits from it — the first says 'what's usual', the second 'how bumpy'. Knowing both, any score can be called 'normal' or 'outrageous' with a straight face.
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: scores [80, 82, 84, 86, 88]. Mean = 84; deviations [−4,−2,0,2,4], mean square = (16+4+0+4+16)/5 = 8, std = √8 ≈ 2.83. A score of 90 sits about 2.1 standard deviations above the mean.
nodes.analogy_zh: 平均分是「平常」，标准差是「波幅」
nodes.analogy_en: The mean is 'usual'; the std is 'bumpiness'

deep.rel_zh: 「几个波动单位」正是显著性语言的地基
deep.rel_en: 'Spread units' ground the language of significance

nodes.one_zh: p 值与置信区间：运气还是真差
nodes.one_en: p-values and confidence intervals
nodes.def_zh: p 值 =「假如根本没有真实差异，光靠运气看到这么大差异」的概率——p 小说明运气很难解释，不是「差异为真的概率」。置信区间 =「真实差异大概落在哪段」的区间估计；含 0 即「说不好方向」。小样本的残酷算术：128 题里一题翻转就是 0.8%，所以小差异必须先过这两道语言关再谈结论。
nodes.def_en: A p-value is the probability of seeing a difference at least this large by pure luck if no real difference exists — a small p means luck struggles to explain it, NOT 'the probability the difference is real'. A confidence interval brackets where the true difference likely lives; containing 0 means 'direction unknowable'. Small-sample arithmetic is brutal: one flipped question out of 128 is 0.8%, so small differences must pass this language before any conclusion.
nodes.plain_zh: 抛硬币连出 5 次正面，能说这硬币偏心吗？先算「好硬币也有多大概率连出 5 次」（这就是 p 值）——三十二分之一，不算稀奇，证据不足。置信区间是另一种说法：「硬币偏心的程度，大概在 −2% 到 +8% 之间，连方向都说不准」。
nodes.plain_en: A coin lands heads five times running — is it biased? First compute how often a fair coin does that (that's the p-value) — 1 in 32, not rare enough, insufficient evidence. The confidence interval says it another way: 'the bias is somewhere between −2% and +8% — we can't even name the direction'.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算：好硬币连出 5 次正面的概率 = (1/2)^5 = 1/32 ≈ 0.031。若事先定显著水平 0.05，p=0.031 < 0.05 才算「运气难解释」。注意方向：p 小 ≠ 结论为真，只 = 该怀疑运气。
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: a fair coin's five straight heads = (1/2)^5 = 1/32 ≈ 0.031. With a significance level fixed at 0.05 beforehand, p=0.031 < 0.05 counts as 'luck strains to explain'. Mind the direction: small p ≠ the claim is true; it only means luck is suspect.
nodes.analogy_zh: 先算好硬币连出五次正面的概率，再谈偏心
nodes.analogy_en: Compute the fair coin's streak first, then accuse bias

deep.rel_zh: 检验的语言建立在均值与波动上
deep.rel_en: The language stands on mean and spread

nodes.one_zh: 任意数据压成固定长度的指纹
nodes.one_en: Any data squeezed to a fixed digest
nodes.def_zh: 哈希函数把任意长度输入映射为固定长度摘要，理想性质：确定性（同输入同输出）、雪崩（改一位全变）、抗碰撞（找两个同摘要的输入极难）。两大用途家族：密码学哈希（SHA-256，身份与完整性）与感知哈希（aHash，相似输入得相近摘要——刻意放弃雪崩换相似性）。从 git 的 commit id 到区块链到文件校验，全是它。
nodes.def_en: A hash function maps arbitrary-length input to a fixed-length digest, ideally deterministic (same input, same output), avalanching (one bit in, everything changes), and collision-resistant (finding two inputs with one digest is infeasible). Two families of use: cryptographic hashes (SHA-256, identity and integrity) and perceptual hashes (aHash, similar inputs yield similar digests — deliberately trading away avalanche for similarity). Git commit ids, blockchains, file checksums — all of it.
nodes.plain_zh: 给任意东西盖一个固定大小的章：一颗钻石和一座山，章都一样大。章的规矩很怪但很好用——东西只动一点点，章面就完全认不出；两个东西章面撞在一起，几乎不可能。
nodes.plain_en: Stamp anything with a fixed-size seal: a diamond and a mountain both get the same seal size. The seal's rules are odd but wonderful — nudge the object a hair and the seal is unrecognizable; two objects landing on the same seal is next to impossible.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算雪崩的味道：sha256('hello') = 2cf24d...，sha256('hellp') 完全不同。终端自试：printf hello | shasum -a 256 与 printf hellp | shasum -a 256 对照。
nodes.example_en: A taste of avalanche: sha256('hello') = 2cf24d... while sha256('hellp') is utterly different. Try it: compare 'printf hello | shasum -a 256' with 'printf hellp | shasum -a 256'.
nodes.analogy_zh: 给钻石和山盖一样大的章，改一点全变样
nodes.analogy_en: One seal size for diamond and mountain; nudge it, all changes

nodes.one_zh: 一组操作要么全成要么全不做
nodes.one_en: All or nothing, as one unit
nodes.def_zh: 事务把一组读写打包成不可分割的单元：提交则全部生效，失败或中断则全部回滚，旁观者永远看不到中间态（ACID 里的 A 与 I）。银行转账是教科书例子：扣款与入账必须同生共死。数据库用它保证崩溃一致性；git 的分支/合并是同一思想在版本控制上的化身（一次合并是一个原子提交）。
nodes.def_en: A transaction bundles reads and writes into an indivisible unit: on commit everything lands, on failure or interrupt everything rolls back, and bystanders never see the middle state (the A and I of ACID). The bank transfer is the textbook case: debit and credit live or die together. Databases use it for crash consistency; git's branch/merge is the same idea incarnated in version control (one merge, one atomic commit).
nodes.plain_zh: 换零钱：把 100 元递出去和收到五个 20 元必须同时发生——递出去一半卡住是最糟糕的。事务就是「这一手要么做完，要么当没发生」，桌上永远不出现半手。
nodes.plain_en: Breaking a 100: handing it over and receiving five 20s must happen together — freezing halfway is the worst outcome. A transaction says 'this move completes or never happened'; a half-move never appears on the table.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算思想实验：转账 = 扣 A 100 + 加 B 100。无事务时第一步后断电 → A 少了 B 没多（钱消失）。有事务时断电 → 两步都当没发生，对账永远平。
nodes.example_en: Thought experiment: a transfer = debit A 100 + credit B 100. Without transactions, power fails after step one → A is poorer, B unchanged (money vanished). With transactions, the failure voids both steps — the books always balance.
nodes.analogy_zh: 换零钱：递出与收进必须同时发生
nodes.analogy_en: Breaking a note: handing over and receiving happen together

nodes.one_zh: 用整数和缩放因子表示小数
nodes.one_en: Decimals as integers times a scale
nodes.def_zh: 定点数用整数 + 约定的缩放因子表示小数：如 22 位定点把 0.5 存成 2097152（0.5×2²¹再取整）。与浮点的区别：定点没有每档不同的指数，算术退化为纯整数运算——在不同 CPU 上结果逐位一致，代价是表示范围与精度固定。凡是「末位差异不可接受」的场合（货币、像素插值、嵌入式）都选它。
nodes.def_en: Fixed-point represents decimals as an integer times an agreed scale: 22-bit fixed-point stores 0.5 as 2097152 (0.5×2²¹, rounded). Unlike floating point there is no per-value exponent — arithmetic degenerates to pure integer math, bit-identical across CPUs, at the price of fixed range and precision. Wherever a last-digit difference is unacceptable (money, pixel interpolation, embedded), fixed-point wins.
nodes.plain_zh: 把「元」全换成「分」来记账：从此只算整数，谁算都一样，绝无「四舍五入到你那儿是一位、到我这儿是另一位」的纠纷。代价是数不了特别大或特别小的数——但像素插值用不着。
nodes.plain_en: Do the books entirely in cents instead of dollars: only integers remain, everyone computes identically, and 'rounds one way on your chip, another way on mine' disputes vanish. The cost: no huge or tiny magnitudes — but pixel interpolation never needed them.
nodes.example_zh: 跟算：22 位定点存 0.5 → 0.5 × 2²¹ = 1048576... 实际按实现取 2²¹ = 2097152 的一半 = 1048576。要点不在具体数：同一公式在同一整数下永远同值——goldmine-embed.c 的 bicubic 靠它逐位钉死。
nodes.example_en: Hand computation: 22-bit fixed-point 0.5 → 0.5 × 2²¹ = 1048576 (half of 2097152). The point isn't the exact number: the same formula on the same integers always yields the same bits — how goldmine-embed.c's bicubic stays bit-exact.
nodes.analogy_zh: 全部用「分」记账，只算整数
nodes.analogy_en: Keep the books in cents; integers only

nodes.one_zh: 给所有文字统一编号的账本
nodes.one_en: One ledger numbering all the world's text
nodes.def_zh: Unicode 给每个字符一个码位（U+0627 是阿拉伯字母 alef）；实际字节流还要经 UTF-8 编码。两个坑与本项目直接相关：①同一文字可有多种码位组合（é 一码位或 e+组合符），规范化（NFC/NFD）负责统一——否则「看起来一样」的词搜不到彼此；②PDF 的文本层靠 ToUnicode 表从字形编号映射回码位，表缺了帖（如阿拉伯 lam-连写），复制出的文字就残缺——这正是丢字病理的根。
nodes.def_en: Unicode assigns every character a code point (U+0627 is the Arabic alef); byte streams encode it via UTF-8. Two traps matter here directly: (1) the same visible text can have several code-point compositions (é as one code point or e plus combining mark) — normalization (NFC/NFD) unifies them, else 'identical-looking' words miss each other in search; (2) a PDF's text layer maps glyph numbers back to code points via ToUnicode tables, and a missing entry (like the Arabic lam-ligature) makes copied text mangled — exactly the root of the lostLetters pathology.
nodes.plain_zh: 全世界的文字共用一本编号账本：「字 → 几号」。麻烦在同一个字可以记好几笔账（一笔记整体、一笔记两个部件），记账方式不统一，账房先生就查不到对方。PDF 的账本还会缺页——缺的那页上的字，抄出来就缺胳膊少腿。
nodes.plain_en: All the world's writing shares one numbered ledger: 'character → number'. Trouble: the same character can be booked two ways (one entry for the whole, or two for the parts); without unifying the bookkeeping, two clerks can't find each other's entries. PDF ledgers can also have missing pages — characters on those pages copy out mangled.
nodes.example_zh: 终端自试：python3 -c "print(len('é'), len('é'))" — 两个看起来一样的 é 长度分别是 1 和 2（组合符），NFC 规范化后才能相等。这正是 normalize_text 存在的理由。
nodes.example_en: Try it: python3 -c "print(len('é'), len('é'))" — two identical-looking é's measure 1 and 2 (combining mark); only NFC normalization makes them equal. That is why normalize_text exists.
nodes.analogy_zh: 全世界文字共用一本编号账本，账本会缺页
nodes.analogy_en: One numbered ledger for all writing — with missing pages

nodes.one_zh: 进程用管道传字节，各有退出码
nodes.one_en: Processes, pipes, buffers, exit codes
nodes.def_zh: 进程 = 一次运行中的程序，有自己的内存与文件描述符；退出码 = 进程结束时给 shell 的一个 0–255 整数（0 惯例为成功；130 = 128+SIGINT）。管道 = 内核里的字节队列，连接两个进程；它有容量上限，写满阻塞、读端关闭后写端得 EPIPE（默认 SIGPIPE 杀进程）。另一关键：语言运行时的用户态缓冲（BufferedReader、stdio 缓冲）会先于内核囤数据——poll 只看得见内核，看不见用户态肚子里的货。
nodes.def_en: A process is a running program with its own memory and file descriptors; an exit code is the 0–255 integer it hands the shell on exit (0 the convention for success; 130 = 128+SIGINT). A pipe is a kernel byte queue joining two processes; it has a capacity cap — writes block when full, and after the read end closes the writer gets EPIPE (SIGPIPE death by default). Another key: language runtimes buffer in userspace (BufferedReader, stdio buffers) and stockpile bytes before the kernel ever sees them — poll sees the kernel, not the goods in userspace stomachs.
nodes.plain_zh: 工厂里的传送带连接两个车间：带子有长度限制（装满就得等），下游下班（读端关闭）后上游再放货就触发警报（EPIPE）。还有个看不见的环节——上游车间内部先有个暂存货架（用户态缓冲），货可能压根没上皮带。每班车结束司机都留一张编号字条（退出码）。
nodes.plain_en: Conveyor belts join two workshops: the belt has a length limit (full means wait), and once the downstream shop closes (read end gone), the next parcel triggers the alarm (EPIPE). There's an invisible link too — the upstream shop has an internal staging rack (userspace buffer), so goods may never have reached the belt at all. Every shift ends with the driver leaving a numbered note (the exit code).
nodes.example_zh: 跟算退出码：python3 -c 'import sys; sys.exit(7)'; echo $? → 7。Ctrl-C 一个前台进程 → echo $? 是 130（128 + 信号 2）。管道容量自试：yes | head -1 秒回——head 读一走，yes 的下一次写就撞 EPIPE。
nodes.example_en: Exit-code drill: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.exit(7)'; echo $? → 7. Ctrl-C a foreground process → echo $? gives 130 (128 + signal 2). Pipe demo: 'yes | head -1' returns instantly — head reads once and leaves; yes's next write hits EPIPE.
nodes.analogy_zh: 车间传送带 + 车内暂存货架 + 班车编号字条
nodes.analogy_en: Workshop belts, an internal staging rack, and numbered shift notes

nodes.one_zh: inode：文件系统里的身份证
nodes.one_en: inode: a file's ID card
nodes.def_zh: 文件系统把「文件」拆成两层：inode（编号 + 大小 + 时间戳 + 权限 + 标志位，存在文件系统表里）与目录项（名字 → inode 的指针）。改名/挪目录只改目录项，inode 不变——这是移动检测的地基。stat/lstat 是读取这层信息的系统调用（stat 跟随符号链，lstat 不）；符号链本身是「存路径的小文件」；macOS 还在 st_flags 里放扩展标志（SF_DATALESS = iCloud 占位）。
nodes.def_en: A filesystem splits 'file' into two layers: the inode (number, size, timestamps, permissions, flag bits, kept in filesystem tables) and directory entries (a name pointing at an inode). Renaming or moving rewrites only the pointer — the inode never changes, which grounds move detection. stat/lstat are the syscalls reading this layer (stat follows symlinks, lstat doesn't); a symlink is itself 'a tiny file holding a path'; macOS further keeps extended flags in st_flags (SF_DATALESS = iCloud placeholder).
nodes.plain_zh: 每辆车有车架号（inode），车牌（文件名）只是贴上去的一块铁皮：换车牌、挪车位，车架号不动——查车架号就知道是同一辆车。符号链是「写着别人家地址的纸条」；有些车的登记信息里还盖着「本体在云端」的特殊章（st_flags）。
nodes.plain_en: Every car has a VIN (the inode); the plate (the filename) is just metal screwed on — swap plates, move parking spots, the VIN stays, and the VIN proves it's the same car. A symlink is 'a note with someone else's address'; some registrations carry a special stamp 'body is in the cloud' (st_flags).
nodes.example_zh: 终端自试：mv a.txt b.txt 前后各跑 ls -i a.txt / ls -i b.txt —— inode 编号不变。stat 与 lstat 的差别：对符号链 ln -s 真文件 链接 跑 stat 链接 与 ls -l 链接，一个报真文件、一个报链接本身。
nodes.example_en: Try it: run 'ls -i a.txt' before and after 'mv a.txt b.txt' — the inode number holds. stat vs lstat: make 'ln -s real link', then 'stat link' versus 'ls -l link' — one reports the real file, the other the link itself.
nodes.analogy_zh: 车架号不动，车牌随便换
nodes.analogy_en: The VIN never moves; plates come and go
